textbookText: 1. SOURCES Major sources of air pollution are illustrated below:

a. Natural sources Dust storms, volcanic gases, emission of natural gases, pollens, spores, methane produced by decaying plants and animal, release of methane trapped in arctic region etc in nature itself cause air pollution. Highest fraction of total pollution about 99.95% is due to natural sources. Only 0.05% of total pollution is due to human activities. However man made population is quite harmful as it is localised in certain area only.

b. Factories Many factories are set up by human beings to meet the increasing demand of increased population. Various factories of food, paper, cement, bricks, shoes, rubber, clothes etc which emit harmful gases viz. CO2, SO2, NO, H2S, CO etc. into the environment.

c. Means of transportation Automobiles, air craft, railways are run by the consumption of fossil fuel and petroleum products. While burning such fuels, harmful gases like CO2, SO2, NO etc. are produced and released to the environment.

d. Metallurgical processing Metallurgical industries have been identified as the contributor to the problem of air pollution since many centuries. During the extraction of metals from ores, smelting and refining processes liberate wastes such as mineral dust, fumes containing fluorid es and the wastes also consist of many hazardous metals like lead, nickel, mercury, arsenic, cobalt, selenium etc.

e. Domestic burning of fuel and waste Various domestic fuels like firewood, kerosene, cooking gases etc. are burnt for household purposes and such activity also releases harmful gases such as CO2, CO etc. containing smoke. Similarly burning of plastics, left over straw in fields by farmers, burning of filth in dumped site, forest fire etc. also contributes to air pollution.
f. Nuclear power plant There may be occasional or accidental release of hazardous radiations like alpha rays, gamma rays from nuclear power plants.
2. EFFECTS OF AIR POLLUTION Various effects of air pollution can be described under following headings:
a. Effects on the environment i. Greenhouse effect:

Gases such as SO2, NO2, CO2, methane, chlofluoro carbon water vapour etc. which trap solar radiation on the earth surface and increase in temperature of earth take place. This phenomenon is called greenhouse effect which is detrimental to the organisms. ii. Acid rain Gases like SO2, NOx, CO2 and other chemicals released from various sources to the atmosphere remain precipitated on the top of buildings, rock, trees and other infrastructures as dry form which later mix and react with rain water to form acid rain. Acid rain water badly affects living beings.

iii. Depletion of ozone layer Some chemicals such as chlorofluoro carbon, methyl chloroform carbon tetrachloride, methyl bromide etc. if present in atmosphere for a long time cause the depletion of ozone layer in stratosphere. Due to which harmful ultraviolet radiations from the sun enter earth surface causing skin and eye problems, cancer, bleaching of living tissues etc. iv. Reduction in visibility Atmosphere becomes unclear due to mixing of smoke, dust particles, fog etc. Due to this objects can’t be seen in polluted environment. v. Reduction in solar radiation Solar radiation is absorbed or blocked by pollutants in air which may increase the temperature of atmosphere.

b. Effects on plants and animals Due to the reduction in solar radiation, stomata of green plants do not open which negatively affects the several plant physiological activities like photosynthesis, respiration and transpiration. Acid rain has detrimental effect on the growth of plants because of mineral and nutrient deficiencies in soil. Less crop yielding, stunted growth of plants, leaves turn yellowish, lichens on tree are also the results of acid rain and air pollution. Aquatic ecosystems will also be disturbed by acid rain. Air pollution brings several health related complications in animals like bronchitis, pneumonia and cardiovascular diseases. Pollutants will also interfere with hormonal secretion in animals leading to reduced gonadial activity, infertility and birth of defective progenies.
